probed_form: Literalize every own readonly f32/f64/string declaration in80346810..80346AAC with a plain literal round-tripping the retail bits; remove the existing volatile-address scalar-read scaffold when it would otherwise take the address of a literal. Initial whole literalization emits660bytes. The unreferenced existing enemy_bss_order helper creates an unwanted leading0.0f; its diagnostic equivalent integer-zero store to the same float storage preserves first-use ordering while producing a168-byte exact prefix. This helper is pre-existing compatibility debt, not evidence of original source.

fn_8004DC2C compares enemy->damage to '(f64)10.0f'; after literalization MWCC promotes the constant and reuses the earlier10.0double. Spelling 'enemy->damage > 10.0f' retains the target single-precision constant load and increases the pool to668bytes. Both compared source values are floats, so dropping these widenings does not change the comparison's mathematical result; other body scheduling still changes.

Immediately before enemy_nearest_live_player, emit the actual29-instruction fn_80034C88 sqrt body already reconstructed in controls.c, with its0.0f/0.5/3.0 literals. Scoped dont_inline prevents accidental caller expansion. Both ordinary and weak definitions preserve the target functions' existing call structure and move3.0double to its retail position, extending the exact prefix to537bytes. Ordinary linkage is a diagnostic only; the weak version is a hypothesis about duplicate/coalesced helper emission, NOT established original linkage.

The only remaining pool differences are0.333 and0.667 in reversed order. In damage_enemy's existing threshold block, compute named f32 lower=(f32)(0.333*threshold) and upper=(f32)(0.667*threshold), passing upper/lower to the existing scale_fight_damage helper. Either declaration order produces the exact668-byte pool. Swapping helper argument order alone, inverting its branch, or adding constant local factors inside the helper leaves the pair reversed.
